archive_info.title: KALAKAR COLLECTIVE
archive_info.subtitle: An Artisans' Archive — Photographic & Oral History Repository of Traditional Sculpture Artisans of India
archive_info.description: An open archive preserving the oral histories, studio photographs, and material records of traditional sculpture artisans of India. Beginning with the rare photographic records of master sculptor Ramesh Singh Kalakar of Begum Bazaar, this archive provides open access to the material culture, economics, and sacred artistry of vernacular craft lineages.

artists.name: Ramesh Singh Kalakar
artists.bio: Pioneering idol artisan and workshop master of Begum Bazaar, Hyderabad. During the 1980s and 1990s, Ramesh’s studio was a crucible of cross-regional artisan collaboration—welcoming master sculptors from Bengal (the Pal lineage) to collaborate with Deccan craftsmen. Famous for monumental scale (up to 22ft), iconic thematic innovations (such as Ganesha depicted as warrior Arjuna and Goddess Durga as Rani Laxmi Bai), intricate handcrafted ornamentation known as "Tickli", and ingenious mechanical kinetic installations featuring motorized roaring lions with hidden audio cassettes.
artists.album_title: Inside Ramesh’s Studio: Begum Bazaar Photographic Records (1980–1990)

artists.name: Dhoolpet Clay Artisans Guild
artists.bio: Generational clay idol makers inhabiting the historic Dhoolpet settlement of Hyderabad, originating from Lodha, Maratha and Bengali migrations. Celebrated for eco-friendly river clay (shadu mati) sculptures and monumental Ganesh Chaturthi festival idols.
artists.album_title: The Clay Alchemists of Dhoolpet (Album Coming Soon)

artists.name: Kumharwadi Terracotta Collective
artists.bio: Traditional potters and ceramic temple craftsmen preserving indigenous Deccan pit-kiln firing techniques, domestic votive terracotta, and festival Bonalu Ghatam decorations.
artists.album_title: Earthen Memory: Kumharwadi Votive Arts (Album Coming Soon)

records.title: Fairy Putting Garlands on Durga Mata
records.concept: The two fairies from the left and right of sky are coming to put the garland on the Goddess Durga. Downwards on the left side the goddess Laxmi and Ganesha praising Durga. Downwards on the right side the goddess Saraswati and Kartikeya praising Durga. The background is made as a sky.
records.material: All the sculptures were made up of Plaster of Paris with the support of Bamboo and wood. The clothes were real, bought from wholesale shop, stitched by his studio persons with the use of nails. The hairs of sculpture were sourced from Kolkata. Ornamentation of sculptures were done by them only; they did not use any readymade jewellery. With the use of artificial beads and gems fixed in clay and saree border designs, they made all the ornamentation things, Mr. Ramesh called it as Tickli. For crown also they used the same Tickli. For shining of sculpture, he used shining paint.
records.other: The empty hands show that when the photograph was captured the sculpture was incomplete. They had to put the weapons in the goddesses hands. The photograph captures the master artisans standing together in front of the 15-foot monumental tableau.

records.title: Nava Durga Fighting Set
records.concept: The goddess Durga and her lion is killing demon. Other sculptures of Laxmi, Saraswati, Ganesh and Kartikeya are placed surrounding it and looking in front.
records.material: All the sculptures were made up of Plaster of Paris with the support of Bamboo and wood. The clothes were real, bought from wholesale shop, stitched by his studio persons with the use of nails. The hairs of sculpture were sourced from Kolkata. Ornamentation of sculptures were done by them only; they did not use any readymade jewellery. With the use of artificial beads and gems fixed in clay and saree border designs, they made all the ornamentation things, Mr. Ramesh called it as Tickli. For crown also they used the same Tickli. For shining of sculpture, he used shining paint. All weapons were made with raw materials like iron sheets and rods which the sculptor fabricated.
records.other: Hand-forged iron sheet weaponry integrated directly into the deity hands before departure to Jagath Girigutta.

records.title: Sculptures for Janamashtami Procession
records.commission_type: Contract from Hare Rama Hare Krishna Foundation
records.concept: The Ganesh murtis were produced for Ganesh Chaturthi and the other sculptures were made for the Krishna Janamashtami procession. The Vishnu sculpture in the center right had dimensions of 9ft. X 7ft. and the Sheshnag sculpture over Vishnu was made with bamboo armature and PoP.
records.material: Plaster of Paris with bamboo and wooden framework. Real garments stitched with nails. Real hair from Kolkata, Tickli ornamentation, and high-gloss paint.
records.other: The patron from Hare Rama Hare Krishna foundation also contracted sculptures for the Tirumala Tirupati temple and Visakhapatnam. Ramesh stayed for a month in Tirupati to make sculptures for the Tirumala Tirupati ground floor temple; those works remain on exhibition there.

records.title: Maa Sherawali and Maa Durga in Exhibition Area
identified_personalities: Ramesh Singh (He died long back ago, not the same person)
records.concept: Both sculptures were made to sell during the Navaratri festival season. Exhibited in the front workshop gallery where clients and festival committees selected their idols.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo, wooden supports, stitched wholesale clothes, Kolkata hair, custom Tickli ornamentation and lacquer shining paint.
records.other: Note on personality: An elder artisan assistant named Ramesh Singh (who passed away long ago, distinct from the studio proprietor Ramesh) is seated in front among the completed murtis.

records.title: Maa Sherawali
records.concept: Maa Sherawali giving blessings (Abhayamudra) to devotees. She sits regally on her vehicle Tiger, holding her foot with one hand while her other hands hold traditional weapons.
records.material: Plaster of Paris with bamboo and wooden core. Sourced Kolkata natural hair, pinned textile drapery, hand-cast Tickli jewel borders, iron weaponry.
records.other: Classic Deccan Navaratri posture showing the dynamic tiger mount with painted stripes and open jaws.

records.title: Bengali Style Maa Durga
records.concept: The Goddess Durga sculpture was crafted in authentic Bengali style because the commissioning committee specifically requested it. Goddess Durga is poised to slay Mahishasura with her trishula while her lion mauls the demon. The ornate stage and two companion sculptures flanking Durga were also custom produced.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo, wood, natural Kolkata hair, Tickli jewel crowns. Background arch (chalchitra) carved out of thick thermocol sheet and hand-painted. Special velour fabric used for lion skin.
records.other: Plaques at bottom show awards won: "Award for Best Pandal 1989". Demonstrates the synthesis of Bengal Daaker Saaj styling within Hyderabad pandal culture.

records.title: Flying Durga Killing the Demon
records.concept: Goddess Durga wears a pristine white saree symbolizing Katyayani, invoked on the sixth day of Navratri where white garments balance martial power with divine peace and maternal grace. The composition depicts her descending from the sky to slay the demon with her attacking lion mount. A third eye on her forehead marks her Shaivite energy.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo armature, white draped silk, Kolkata hair, Tickli crowns, high-gloss enamel paints.
records.other: Sculpted in a suspended aerial posture. At the time of this studio photograph, the hand weapons had not yet been fixed into the fingers.

records.title: Shankar’s Family (Shiva Parivar Tableau)
records.concept: Monumental tableau depicting Lord Shiva holding child Kartikeya and Goddess Durga as Parvati holding baby Ganesha while seated on her lion. Parvati is shown with only two hands and without weapons, emphasizing domestic serenity and motherhood. Shiva sits atop Nandi (partially hidden behind).
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo, wooden armature. Real fabrics pinned with nails. Natural Kolkata hair, handmade Tickli ornaments. Kinetic motor mechanism and audio playback.
records.other: Mechanical innovation: The lion head was crafted from papier-mâché and fitted with an internal electric motor designed by Ramesh, oscillating its head left to right with lifelike hair movement. An internal cassette tape recorder played an authentic recording of a lion roar. Ramesh recalled finding a cassette with an isolated lion roar was an immense challenge at that time.

records.title: Durga Mata with Ganesha & Kartikeya
records.concept: Five-sculpture set featuring Goddess Durga holding Ganesha on her left, flanked by her roaring Lion, Kartikeya, and Ganesha’s vahana Mushaka. Durga is sculpted with ten arms and Ganesha with four.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo framework, rich brocade textiles, Kolkata hair, Tickli jewels, shining paint.
records.other: The empty hands reveal that the piece was photographed in the workshop just before final weapon assembly for delivery to the Langar House pandal.

records.title: The Cycle of Life (Human Metamorphosis)
records.commission_type: Contract from Hare Rama Hare Krishna Foundation
records.concept: An extraordinary philosophical suite of twelve graduated human figures illustrating the transmigration and cycle of human life from infant birth to old age and death, commissioned for the spiritual museum in Tirupati.
records.material: Fine Plaster of Paris, custom cloth dhotis, lifelike human anatomy modeling, naturalistic flesh tones.
records.other: Ramesh stayed for a month on site in Tirupati to assemble and install this set, which became a permanent exhibition at Tirumala Tirupati temple.

records.title: Goddess Durga with Devotee / Studio Portrait
records.concept: Goddess Durga seated on her tiger mount with green satin garment. Posed with studio family member Meenakshi Bai seated gracefully on the floor beside the tiger.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, tiger armature, green satin with gold borders, natural hair, hand-painted eyes.
records.other: Historic temporal marker: On the studio floor next to Meenakshi Bai lies a copy of The Times dated to late 2000 reporting the Bush vs Gore US presidential contest, providing an irreplaceable ethnographic timestamp for the workshop records.

records.title: Vaishno Devi in Siddhipet
identified_personalities: Businessman and Pandit in Siddhipet (patrons in photo)
records.concept: Goddess Durga sculpted under the theological influence of Vaishno Devi Pindi. Commissioned by a prominent devotee merchant and priest from Siddhipet who traveled to Begum Bazaar every single year to commission their centerpiece murti.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo structure, multi-tiered carved throne, ceremonial offerings and silver foil backdrops.
records.other: The photograph depicts the Siddhipet businessman and pandit performing the consecration puja with lit brass lamps and coconut offerings inside the pandal.

records.title: Ganesha as Arjun (Warrior on Chariot)
records.concept: Goddess Ganesha portrayed as the heroic Mahabharata archer Arjun, standing atop a galloping horse-drawn war chariot. Ramesh Sir intentionally envisioned Ganesha with muscular pehelwaan (wrestler) physique rather than traditional rotund belly, holding a bow and ready for battle.
records.material: Colossal PoP structure, heavy timber framework, sculpted white horses, golden chariot chariot-wheels, real dhoti with brocade borders.
records.other: Standing over 20 feet tall, this monumental installation became a legendary landmark at Begum Bazar Chatri. Elder brother Sheetal Singh stands proudly beside the chariot.

records.title: Durga Mata as Rani Laxmi Bai
records.concept: Revolutionary iconographic synthesis: Goddess Durga portrayed as the freedom fighter Rani Laxmi Bai of Jhansi astride a rearing white stallion, with baby Ganesha seated beside her on the saddle. She wears military soldier attire with high black cavalry riding boots and brandishes a curved talwar sword while subduing the demon.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo, custom stitched equestrian soldier garments, black boots, golden crowns, hand-forged sword.
records.other: A bold nationalist-devotional crossover that drew enormous crowds at Jagat Giri Gutta during festival days.

records.title: Ganesh with Riddhi and Siddhi
records.concept: Lord Ganesha seated majestically in royal court attire, flanked by his consorts Riddhi (prosperity) and Siddhi (spiritual attainment) holding chauris (flywhisks).
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo framework, rich brocade and satin sashes, Kolkata hair, Tickli crowns.
records.other: Captured in the back studio bay while final touches on the facial expressions and crown ornaments were underway.

records.title: Flying Durga and Ganesha Killing Demons
records.concept: Dynamic aerial battle composition: Goddess Durga and a child-warrior Ganesha swooping down together from the clouds to confront and overpower demonic adversaries.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, suspended bamboo armatures, red silk sarees, hand-molded Tickli jewelry.
records.other: Displays the workshop mastery of cantilevered, gravity-defying postures that made Ramesh’s Begum Bazaar studio famous.

records.title: Hairy Hanuman Roop (Veer Hanuman with Rama & Lakshmana)
records.concept: Monumental kneeling Hanuman with authentic textured fur modeling throughout his body, carrying Lord Rama and Prince Lakshmana tenderly upon his shoulders.
records.material: Plaster of Paris with specialized rough stippling and jute hair application for lifelike fur texture; hand-painted gold armor and crown.
records.other: The use of fibrous textures on the Pop skin gives the impression of a living primate deity, a breakthrough technique in 1980s Hyderabad sculpture.

records.title: Vasudev Carrying Baby Krishna Across Yamuna
identified_personalities: Jai Singh (now proprietor of photo framing shop)
records.concept: Vasudev wading across the stormy waters of river Yamuna carrying basket with newborn baby Krishna on his head, sheltered from the torrents by the multi-headed serpent king Sheshnag rising like a cosmic parasol.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo and wire mesh armature for serpent hoods, silver and white drapery, painted surging waves.
records.other: Artisan assistant Jai Singh (who later established a photo framing business in Hyderabad) is visible in the studio records. Part of the landmark Tirupati spiritual pavilion.

records.title: Ganesha as Krishna Stealing Makhan (Makhan Chor)
records.concept: Playful mythological amalgamation: Lord Ganesha portrayed in the role of mischievous child Krishna climbing atop friends to steal fresh churned butter (makhan) from hanging earthen pots, while the gopis look up in delighted astonishment.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, bamboo scaffolding, realistic hanging pots, satin clothes pinned with studio nails, Tickli jewelry.
records.other: Transported and installed for the annual festival celebrations in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh.

records.title: Radha Krishna and Ram Darbar Studio Assembly
records.concept: A dual devotional court: on the left, divine lovers Radha and Krishna seated with sacred Kamadhenu cow and royal peacock; on the right, the grand Ram Darbar with Lord Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Bharata, Shatrughna and kneeling devotee Hanuman.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, glistening satin silks, custom crafted mukuts (crowns), studio paint pots and raw terracotta models on floor.
records.other: Vividly documents studio workspace conditions: paint mixing buckets, wooden scaffolding, stools, and miniature raw clay Ganeshas drying on the workshop floor.

records.title: Shankar’s Family (Finished Full-Color Installation)
records.concept: The completed, fully painted and regally outfitted companion to the process photograph in Record #8. Lord Shiva in tiger pelt holding infant Kartikeya, and Goddess Parvati in crimson-gold sari crowned with intricate Tickli mukut holding Ganesha atop the roaring paper-mache lion.
records.material: Plaster of Paris, kinetic paper-mache lion with integrated motor and lion-roar cassette recorder, gold sequin embroidery, Kolkata natural hair.
records.other: This photograph captures the finished masterpiece under festival canopy lighting in all its theatrical grandeur, with the lion jaws wide open and the motor mechanism running.
